name: WACO 9 / 10 / GXE
variants: Various radial and V-engine versions, 90 to 330 hp
summary: The most numerous Waco, with over 1,600 built; the barnstorming workhorse of the late 1920s.

wings: Single-bay staggered biplane with straight, untapered wings
Ailerons on both upper and lower wings, strut-linked
engines: Curtiss OX-5 water-cooled V-8 with a nose radiator on the GXE, or an air-cooled radial on later versions
fuselage: Two open cockpits with the passenger cockpit under the upper wing ahead of the pilot
Split-axle fixed tailwheel gear with hydraulic shock absorbers

tellTales: Biplane with a passenger cockpit ahead of the pilot, under the wing
Straight, untapered wings with strut-linked ailerons on both wings
Water-cooled V-8 with a front radiator or an exposed radial

confusedWith.howToTell: The Taperwing's wings taper toward the tips; the Waco 10's wings are straight.
The F-series is a later, more streamlined design with a radial engine and wide-track gear; the Waco 10 is a boxier barnstormer often with a nose radiator.
The Travel Air has big overhanging balanced ailerons; the Waco 10 ailerons are strut-linked without big horns.
The Stearman is larger with a bare radial and a narrower front cockpit; the Waco 10's front cockpit is wide and under the wing.
